document_title: Nobody at the wheel on Interstate 45
_note: Built from render_report.json's own text_nodes rather than retyped, because the strings a reader receives are the ones the browser laid out. The sheet on frame 6 is drawn on a canvas as unlabelled rows and ticks, one per acknowledgement, and carries no words.

S1.headline: Nobody at the wheel
S1.body: Kodiak plans unsupervised driverless service on the Dallas to Houston lane by the end of 2026. Aurora said investor day guests could ride part of its route with nobody behind the wheel.
strings: Kodiak plans unsupervised driverless service on the Dallas to Houston lane by the end of 2026. Aurora said investor day guests could ride part of its route with nobody behind the wheel.

S2.headline: 219 miles, Kodiak says
S2.body: That is Kodiak's figure for the Dallas-Fort Worth and Houston metros along Interstate 45. Waabi hauls the same corridor and calls it roughly 240.
strings: That is Kodiak's figure for the Dallas-Fort Worth and Houston metros along Interstate 45. Waabi hauls the same corridor and calls it roughly 240.

S3.headline: Hands off the wheel
S3.body: A safety observer rides on Kodiak's deliveries from Lancaster to Houston. Kodiak says the observer never touched the wheel.
strings: A safety observer rides on Kodiak's deliveries from Lancaster to Houston. Kodiak says the observer never touched the wheel.

S4.headline: 35 already ran with nobody in the cab
S4.body: Kodiak says 35 driverless trucks were running commercially in its Permian Basin industrial deployment with no humans in the cab at the end of the second quarter.
strings: 35 already ran with nobody in the cab
Kodiak says 35 driverless trucks were running commercially in its Permian Basin industrial deployment with no humans in the cab at the end of the second quarter.

S5.headline: 200 by year end, 20 reported
S5.body: Aurora says it is fully allocated to end 2026 with 200 driverless trucks. Breitbart puts the fleet running now at 20. It cites a CNBC ride.
strings: Aurora says it is fully allocated to end 2026 with 200 driverless trucks. Breitbart puts the fleet running now at 20. It cites a CNBC ride.

S6.headline: Six conditions and no fee
S6.body: Since May 28th a commercial driverless operator needs a TxDMV authorization. It is free, it does not expire, and it rests on a statement with six conditions and a responder plan.
strings: Since May 28th a commercial driverless operator needs a TxDMV authorization. It is free, it does not expire, and it rests on a statement with six conditions and a responder plan.

S7.headline: Dallas asked for crash history
S7.body: The department said Transportation Code § 545.453 and § 545.456 do not allow it to require crash history from authorization holders. A required recording device is among the acknowledgements.
strings: The department said Transportation Code § 545.453 and § 545.456 do not allow it to require crash history from authorization holders. A required recording device is among the acknowledgements.

S8.headline: The line is serious bodily injury
S8.cite: c13 to c17 c38 DRAWN TO SCALE
S8.body: The department counts an operation as endangering the public when it has caused or is likely to cause serious bodily injury. Below that line it says administrative action is unlikely. Roadside enforcement belongs to DPS and local law enforcement.
strings: The line is serious bodily injury

S9.headline: Where to report one
S9.body: A concern about a driverless vehicle that could cause serious bodily injury or death can be sent for review to the TxDMV Enforcement Division. Its address txmccs.txdmv.gov/truckstop is also where law enforcement can verify authorizations.
